title: App Development Company Manchester | 22 Signals
description: An app development company Manchester firms use for iOS, Android and web apps: MVPs, payments, APIs and app store launch, with one lead and dates in writing.
h1: App development company Manchester businesses use to ship, not stall
intro: We build iOS and Android apps, web apps and SaaS products for established Manchester companies and the founders they back. That covers scoping a first version, design, development, payments, APIs, app store launch and support afterwards. You get one accountable lead, a dated plan and an app your customers or staff actually keep using.

sections.h: Most app projects fail before a line of code
p: The usual story: a Manchester company decides it needs an app, writes a feature list as long as a menu, gets three quotes that differ by a factor of four, and picks the middle one. Eighteen months later the app is half built, the original developer has moved on, and nobody can say whether customers even wanted it.

We start somewhere else. What job does the app do for the user, what is the smallest version that does it, and how will you know it is working? Answer those, and the build becomes far more predictable.

In practice, the real need for a Manchester company is often narrower than the first brief: a staff app that replaces a paper process, or a customer app that does one thing better than the website. Starting there gets something useful into people's hands sooner, and the feature list can grow from evidence rather than guesswork.

sections.h: UK data, children's privacy and financial rules
p: Apps collect more personal data than most websites: location, contacts, photos, health readings, payment details. UK GDPR and the Data Protection Act 2018 apply to all of it, and we design permissions, storage and deletion around those rules. If your app is likely to be used by under-18s, the ICO's Age Appropriate Design Code, often called the Children's Code, sets extra standards. The ICO, based in Wilmslow just south of Manchester, has enforced it actively, so it is worth taking seriously from the first wireframe.

Financial apps carry further duties. If you are FCA authorised, the Consumer Duty affects how the app explains products and treats customers. We build with your compliance team rather than around them.

It is relevant here because it is exactly the kind of build where scope, performance and testing with real users decide whether a product works, and that is how we run app projects for clients.

sections.h: An app development company Manchester clients can work with remotely
p: We are based in London with no Manchester office, and that suits app work well. Builds run on short cycles: you install the latest test version, try it, and send feedback the same day. Manchester and London share a time zone, so stand-ups and reviews sit inside normal working hours for both sides.

Some moments are better face to face, such as the initial product workshop or user testing with your customers. Your Signal Lead travels up from London for those when the project needs it; it is about two hours by train.

faqs.q: Should we build native or cross-platform?
faqs.a: For most business apps, a cross-platform framework such as React Native or Flutter gives you iOS and Android from one codebase, which saves time and keeps features in step. Native makes sense for heavy graphics, deep hardware use or very specific platform features. We recommend after understanding what the app must do.

faqs.q: Can you take over an app another agency started?
faqs.a: Often, yes. We start with a code and infrastructure review to see what is reusable, what is risky and what is missing, then give you an honest recommendation: continue, refactor or rebuild parts. You get the findings in writing before committing to anything further.

faqs.q: Do you meet app clients in Manchester?
faqs.a: When the project needs it. Product workshops and user testing sessions can be worth doing in person, and your Signal Lead travels from London for them. The rest of the project runs remotely in UK hours, with test builds on your phone at the end of each cycle.

faqs.q: Do we need an app development company Manchester-based to get a good result?
faqs.a: Not really. What matters is how often you see working software, how quickly feedback turns into changes and who is accountable for dates. Those depend on process, not postcode. We share your time zone, put a new test build on your phone every cycle, and come to Manchester in person when a workshop or user test needs it.

faqs.q: How do you handle UK GDPR in an app?
faqs.a: We ask only for the permissions the app needs, explain why at the moment we ask, store data securely and in the right region, and give users a way to see and delete their data. If children may use the app, we apply the ICO's Children's Code. Your data protection lead gets documentation to review.

faqs.q: Who owns the app and the code?
faqs.a: We agree that in writing before the build starts, covering the code repository, app store accounts, cloud hosting and design files, and you always have access to what we build and run for you. We document it so another team could pick it up if you ever needed them to.

faqs.q: What happens after the app is in the stores?
faqs.a: Apple and Google change their rules and operating systems every year, so apps need regular updates. We offer support plans covering updates, crash monitoring, security patches and small improvements, and we can plan the next features based on how people actually use the app.
